name: T-Hybrid Generation
tagline: T-Hybrid: 541 PS, an eTurbo and 400 volts
description:
The 992.2 is the first 911 generation to carry a high-voltage electrical system, and Porsche's engineers arrived at the shortest possible route to it. Unveiled on 28 May 2024 alongside the revived Carrera, the debut model was the Carrera GTS with the T-Hybrid system: a 3.6-litre boxer with a single electrically assisted exhaust-gas turbocharger, a permanent-magnet synchronous motor buried inside the eight-speed PDK, and a 1.9 kWh, 400-volt battery no bigger than a conventional starter battery. The motor spins the turbo to speed before the exhaust gas arrives, so boost is instant — full system torque of 610 Nm is on tap below 2,000 rpm. Unlike a plug-in hybrid, the battery is never drained for propulsion; it is there to recover energy and to fill gaps. Porsche cites a weight penalty of just 50 kg over the outgoing GTS, against roughly eight times that for a typical PHEV.

The Carrera line was re-cut around the new powertrain. The base 992.2 Carrera keeps a 2,981 cc twin-turbo six — now with the old GTS turbochargers and Turbo-type intercooling for 394 PS — while the long-absent Carrera S returned in January 2025 with 480 PS, closing the gap to the old 992.1 GTS. All-wheel drive came back in July 2025 with the 473 hp Carrera 4S Coupé and Cabriolet and the Targa 4S, bringing the AWD count to six. There is deliberately no base Carrera 4: Porsche states the standard Carrera is not offered with all-wheel drive. The Turbo S followed at IAA Munich in September 2025, taking the T-Hybrid to its extreme with two eTurbos, 711 PS, 322 km/h and a 7:03.92 Nürburgring Nordschleife lap — about 14 seconds quicker than the 992.1 car despite carrying 85 kg more.

Running the other way from the hybrids, the GT3 doubled down on what it always was. The 2025 GT3 and GT3 Touring retained the 4.0-litre naturally aspirated six at 510 PS and a 9,000 rpm redline, survived Euro 7 with two particulate filters and four catalytic converters at the cost of 20 Nm, and compensated with a final drive 8 per cent shorter than before. The Weissach Package became available on a non-RS GT3 for the first time. On 14 April 2026 the GT3 S/C arrived — the first open-top GT3 in history, manual-only, two-seater, and the lightest open-top 911 in the range. For the manual faithful, the Carrera T arrived as the only three-pedal 911 below the GT3, and in August 2026 Porsche restored a manual Carrera S to North America as an MT Package exclusive.

One open question remains at the close of 2026: no 992.2 GT3 RS has been announced. Prototypes have been photographed at the Nürburgring since mid-2025, and spy photographers read the exhaust note as turbocharged, but Porsche has published nothing. The roster entry is retained and marked unconfirmed rather than guessed. Alongside the range, Porsche's collector arm has been busy — the Spirit 70 (1,500), the GT3 90 F. A. Porsche (90) and the ten individually configured Carrera 4 GTS Tribute to Transfăgărășan cars.

variants.description: The 992.2 Carrera was the entry point to the T-Hybrid era, unveiled on 28 May 2024 in Coupé and Cabriolet form. Its 2,981 cc twin-turbo flat-six keeps the previous GTS turbochargers and adopts the charge-air cooler from the outgoing Turbo, lifting output to 290 kW (394 PS; 388 hp) and 450 Nm while cutting emissions. Performance is 4.1 s to 100 km/h — 3.9 s with the Sport Chrono Package — and 294 km/h (183 mph). The Cabriolet gives up 2 km/h and 0.2 s. variants.description: With the Carrera S gone PDK-only, the T became the only three-pedal 911 below the GT3 — and for the first time the manual-only model is also offered as a Cabriolet. It uses the base Carrera's 2,981 cc twin-turbo six (394 PS / 388 hp, 450 Nm) but sheds weight: 1,490 kg DIN in Coupé form makes it the lightest 992.2, 30 kg below the Carrera. Rear-axle steering, PASM dampers tuned specifically for the T and an open-pore laminated-walnut gear knob come as standard, and 70 per cent of 992.1 T buyers already chose the manual. At 4.5 s to 100 km/h it is the slowest 992.2 Coupé, which is rather the point.

variants.description: Porsche re-created the Carrera S in January 2025 to slot between the Carrera and the hybrid GTS, delivering the performance of the outgoing 992.1 GTS without the 3.6-litre engine. The 2,981 cc twin-turbo six gained 30 hp to 353 kW (480 PS; 473 hp) and 530 Nm thanks to new turbochargers and intercooling carried over from the 911 Turbo. Coupé and Cabriolet are offered, both with the eight-speed PDK only — the manual version returned to North America a year and a half later as the separate MT Package car. With Sport Chrono the Coupé reaches 100 km/h in 3.3 s and 308 km/h (191 mph).

It adopts the upgraded Carrera S engine — 473 hp (353 kW) and 390 lb-ft, up 30 hp — with charge-air cooling taken from the 911 Turbo, and an eight-speed PDK sending power to all four wheels. variants.description: The first road-legal 911 with a performance hybrid, revealed on 28 May 2024 and in production from June. A single wastegate-free eTurbo replaces the old twin-turbo arrangement: its motor sits between compressor and turbine, spinning the shaft instantly and doubling as an 11 kW generator. The 3.6-litre boxer (bore grew 6 mm, stroke 4.6 mm) is 110 mm shallower because the belt drive is gone, freeing space for the inverter and DC-DC converter. The PDK motor adds up to 150 Nm and 40 kW from idle. Nürburgring time: 7:16.93, some 8.7 s quicker than the 992.1 GTS despite 47 kg more mass. Only 50 kg of the hybrid is real penalty.

variants.description: Revealed on 18 October 2024 as a 25th-anniversary double premiere, the 992.2 GT3 launched simultaneously with a fixed rear wing and as a wingless Touring Package car. Porsche consulted some 2,000 GT3 owners before developing it, and the brief was clear: no turbos, no batteries, no drive modes. Meeting Euro 7 while keeping the naturally aspirated flat-six cost 20 Nm — down from 470 to 450 Nm — with revised cylinder heads, camshafts from the GT3 RS, flow-optimised throttle bodies and better oil coolers doing the work. Power and the 9,000 rpm redline are unchanged. The Weissach Package, previously reserved for the RS, is available for the first time on a standard GT3, and the Clubsport package is offered at no cost.

variants.description: For the first time the GT3 Touring Package was available from launch rather than as a later arrival, and the designation traces back to the 1973 Carrera RS 2.7. Dropping the fixed swan-neck wing for an extendable spoiler with a Gurney flap and revised underbody fins restores the classic 911 roofline — the drop in drag is why the manual Touring, at 313 km/h, outruns the winged PDK car at 311 km/h. The Lightweight Package adds a body-coloured CFRP roof, CFRP anti-roll bar, coupling rods and rear shear panel, forged magnesium wheels, lightweight door panels and the shortened S/T gear lever. All GT3 mechanicals are shared, including the 9,000 rpm flat-six.

The roster entry is retained as a placeholder and deliberately carries no 992.2 specifications. What is on record: prototypes of a 992.2-phase GT3 RS have been photographed testing at the Nürburgring since mid-2025, most recently in September 2026, with a revised front bumper, canards, a wider diffuser and a three-element active rear wing retaining DRS. Spy photography and soundtrack recordings have led outlets to conclude forced induction is likely, with power estimates from 650 hp upward, but Porsche GT boss Andreas Preuninger has only said a turbocharged or electrified future GT3 is possible. Reveal dates reported for August 2026 did not materialise. The current on-sale car remains the 992.1 GT3 RS.

variants.engine: 2,981 cc (3.0 L) twin-turbocharged flat-six, 91.0 × 76.4 mm (992.2 Carrera S unit)
variants.weight: 3,327 lb (1,509 kg) curb weight, Coupé — only 11 lb above the Carrera T Coupé
variants.drivetrain: Rear-wheel drive (manual offered exclusively with rear-wheel drive)
variants.transmission: 6-speed manual only (shared with the 911 Carrera T)
variants.description: Appended variant. Announced on 13 August 2026 and debuting at Monterey Car Week, the MT Package brings a six-speed manual Carrera S back to North America for the first time since 2019 — the 992.2 had launched PDK-only. North America is the sole market, and the package adds a higher specification than the PDK Carrera S while minimising weight: Sport Chrono, rear-axle steering, GT Sport steering wheel and larger brakes are standard, and carbon-fibre bucket seats and PCCB are optional — the last of which is not available on the Carrera T. Curb weight is 3,327 lb in Coupé form. US pricing starts at $167,100 for the Coupé and $181,000 for the Cabriolet.

variants.engine: T-Hybrid: 3,591 cc (3.6 L) turbocharged flat-six with single eTurbo + PM synchronous motor in the PDK; 400 V / 1.9 kWh battery (992.2 Carrera 4 GTS basis)
variants.power: 398 kW (541 PS; 532 hp) system output — mechanically unchanged from the Carrera 4 GTS
variants.torque: 610 Nm (450 lb-ft; 449 lb-ft US) system torque
variants.acceleration: 3.0 s (0–100 km/h; 0–60 mph 2.9 s with Sport Chrono Package)
variants.transmission: 8-speed PDK dual-clutch with integrated electric motor
variants.description: Appended variant. Ten individually configured 992.2 Carrera 4 GTS Coupés built through the Porsche Sonderwunsch programme to celebrate 50 years of the Transfăgărășan, the 90-kilometre Romanian mountain road that also marked the 911 Turbo's 50th in 2024. Each car carries 'Tribute to Transfăgărășan' door decals, a special B-pillar badge, engine-grille slats in the Romanian blue-yellow-red, illuminated door sill guards, embroidered headrests and an embossed centre armrest. The hero car, in Paint to Sample Graphite Grey with Guards Red wheel spokes and headlight rings, was delivered in August 2025 and driven straight onto the road it honours. No mechanical changes were made.
variants.production: 10 cars, each individually specified by its owner with the Sonderwunsch and Style Porsche teams (first delivered August 2025)

variants.description: Appended variant. Created by the Sonderwunsch team with designer F. A. Porsche's son Mark to mark what would have been the 90th birthday of Ferdinand Alexander Porsche on 11 December 2025 — and based on the one-off GT3 Touring that Porsche had already built as a birthday present. Ninety cars worldwide, one of them Mark Porsche's. The paint is F. A. Greenmetallic, developed with the family and inspired by the Oakgreenmetallic of F. A.'s own 911; satin black Sport Classic wheels carry the historic 1963 crest; Truffle Brown Club leather, open-pore walnut and a five-colour F. A. Grid-Weave seat fabric (a reference to his favourite jackets) fill the cabin. Each car ships with a titanium Porsche Design Chronograph 1. German price: €351,211; US MSRP $387,000.
variants.production: 90 units worldwide (one reserved for Mark Porsche); orderable from April 2026, production from mid-2026
